[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Network Configuration in Linux"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covers essential network configuration tools in Linux: 'ifconfig', 'ip', 'route', and 'netstat/ss'. Understanding these tools is crucial for managing network interfaces, routing, and network statistics."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Interface Configuration: ifconfig (Deprecated)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"'ifconfig' (interface configuration) was a traditional tool for configuring network interfaces. While still available on some systems, it's largely superseded by the 'ip' command. It's used to assign IP addresses, netmasks, and other interface parameters."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"# Display all active network interfaces:
sudo ifconfig"},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"# Assign an IP address and netmask to eth0:
sudo ifconfig eth0 192.168.1.10 netmask 255.255.255.0"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"# Bring an interface up or down:
sudo ifconfig eth0 up
sudo ifconfig eth0 down"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Interface Configuration: ip (Modern)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'ip' command is the modern replacement for 'ifconfig' and provides a more powerful and versatile way to manage network interfaces, routing, and tunnels."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"# Display all network interfaces:
ip addr show"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Assign an IP address to eth0:
sudo ip addr add 192.168.1.10/24 dev eth0"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"# Bring an interface up or down:
sudo ip link set eth0 up
sudo ip link set eth0 down"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"# Show interface statistics:
ip -s link show eth0"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Routing Table Management: route"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'route' command is used to display and manipulate the kernel's IP routing table. It allows you to add, delete, and modify routes, directing network traffic to the correct destinations."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Display the routing table:
sudo route -n"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"# Add a default gateway:
sudo route add default gw 192.168.1.1"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"# Add a route to a specific network:
sudo route add -net 10.0.0.0/24 gw 192.168.1.1"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"# Delete a route:
sudo route del -net 10.0.0.0/24"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Routing Table Management: ip route"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'ip route' command is the modern way to manage the routing table, offering more features and flexibility than the traditional 'route' command."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"# Display the routing table:
ip route show"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"# Add a default gateway:
sudo ip route add default via 192.168.1.1"},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"# Add a route to a specific network:
sudo ip route add 10.0.0.0/24 via 192.168.1.1"},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"# Delete a route:
sudo ip route del 10.0.0.0/24"},{"order":26,"type":"subheading","text":"Network Statistics: netstat (Deprecated)"},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"'netstat' (network statistics) was a traditional tool for displaying network connections, routing tables, interface statistics, masquerade connections, and multicast memberships. It's largely superseded by the 'ss' command."},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"# Display all active network connections:
sudo netstat -a"},{"order":29,"type":"code","text":"# Display listening ports:
sudo netstat -l"},{"order":30,"type":"code","text":"# Display routing table:
sudo netstat -r"},{"order":31,"type":"subheading","text":"Network Statistics: ss (Modern)"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'ss' (socket statistics) command is the modern replacement for 'netstat'. It provides more detailed and efficient information about network sockets and connections."},{"order":33,"type":"code","text":"# Display all active network connections:
ss -a"},{"order":34,"type":"code","text":"# Display listening ports:
ss -l"},{"order":35,"type":"code","text":"# Display TCP connections:
ss -t"},{"order":36,"type":"code","text":"# Display UDP connections:
ss -u"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"By mastering these tools, you can effectively manage and troubleshoot network configurations in Linux systems. Remember to use 'ip' and 'ss' as your primary tools, as they are the modern and recommended replacements for 'ifconfig' and 'netstat'."}]
